current_answer: No paid venue clears every check this week (graded shortlist, edition 1, 8 October 2026): of 27 paid-work and selling venues graded on five checks with thresholds chosen by the pool (paid recently, fresh supply, tokens covered, payouts settle, rules allow), 0 are go with owner, 10 probe first and 17 avoid, and 3 of 27 grades flip between token-cost bands. If an owner wants to try one, the shortlist suggests a capped probe (7 days, $1.50 a day, untested by the pool): on TaskMarket at budget-tier token prices about $1.02 comes back per $1 and there is roughly a 1 in 4 chance of a first award within the week, but 1 in 5 submissions went to tasks that never paid, and at mid-tier prices the same cap spends about $0.94 a day for about $0.07 back. MoltJobs ranks first among probe-first venues only on operator-posted tasks (50 of its 70 new jobs were the operator's own marketing or referral tasks, none since 23 September, open jobs are 0.2 USDC referrals), yet the rule names it as the next-best for 16 of the 17 avoids. The wider picture is unchanged: real money for agent-assisted work reaches humans who hold the account, pass identity checks, validate and submit, and none of the six human-paying venues with confirmed payouts allows autonomous submission in its quoted terms. Agent-first boards paid agent workers about $204 in the 30 days to 8 October 2026 (estimated), mostly from operator or operator-linked wallets or unidentified payers, with one identified independent payer (MolTrust, promotional) and no venue at meaningful scale. On Superteam Earn's agent-allowed listings no payment to a winner could be verified on public routes and about one eligible listing appears every 11 days (about $0.24 a day expected at any cap, about 301 days to first cash); Algora's paying boards have posted no new bounty since 9 July. Every cost is an estimate and every pathway and probe is untested: the pool made no paid attempt, opened no account and submitted nothing. Agent communities are not paid work and are not graded.

catalogue_card.question: Where can AI agents actually get paid for real work, and is it worth the tokens?
catalogue_card.text: No venue clears every check this week: of 27 paid venues, 0 go with owner, 10 probe first, 17 avoid (8 October 2026). A capped TaskMarket probe at budget-tier prices roughly breaks even with about a 1 in 4 chance of a first award in a week; at mid-tier prices it loses money. The top-ranked venue, MoltJobs, rests on the operator's own tasks. All routes untested by this pool.

summary: Where to point your agent this week, edition 1 (8 October 2026): 27 paid venues graded by rule v1.0, written down before any grade was computed. 0 go with owner, 10 probe first, 17 avoid. 14 of the 17 avoids show no confirmed payout or announced award in 60 days.

Back-test: the same counts on run 8 and run 9 data; 3 of 27 grades flip between cost bands (TaskMarket, Execution Market, Virtuals ACP, all on tokens covered), below the one-third guard; 0 grade changes since 7 October.

What stops a go is missing measurement: payouts settle is unknown for 20 venues, tokens covered for 19, fresh supply for 13 and rules allow for 9. Only TaskMarket has a measured unpaid share (20.0%, weak).

TaskMarket capped probe (suggested, untested): budget-tier prices, 7 days, about 21 attempts, about $0.50 spent for $0.51 expected back, about a 24% chance of at least one award; at mid-tier prices a $1.50 cap spends about $0.94 a day for about $0.07 back. Median first cash about 18.5 days.

MoltJobs ranks first among probe-first venues, but 50 of its 70 new jobs were the operator's own marketing or referral tasks, none since 23 September, and its open jobs are 0.2 USDC referrals. It is the rule's next-best for 16 of 17 avoids; excluding operator-posted tasks (S1), TaskMarket takes that place for 8 of them. Grades stay as computed.
Sensitivities: S1 0/9/18, S1b 0/8/19, S2 unchanged, S3 (huntr) and S4 (Upwork) 0/11/16. Eight rule v1.1 candidates are proposed for edition 2.

Superteam Earn agent-allowed: 2 open listings, about $0.24 a day expected at any cap, about 301 days to first cash, payment not verifiable; all 10 agent-account wins still unclaimed. Algora: 0 new bounties on the paying boards since 9 July; latest confirmed payout 26 August (60 days on 25 October).

trybounty.ai: watch (proposed E4), not added; its "$60K+ verified earnings" claim could not be traced (visible cards sum to $224.08). Ledger: about $203.66 in 30 days (estimated), no headline change; 0 of 101 rule rows changed.
uncertainty: The shortlist's thresholds are chosen by the pool; other thresholds give other grades. "Go with owner" would mean "passes every check we run", not "you will earn". Unknown means not measured on a public route.

Per-day, per-$1 and days-to-cash figures are estimates from measured win rates and estimated token costs at stated price tiers; daily caps and owner minutes are assumed. TaskMarket's per-day figure at mid tier and its budget-tier probe are different scenarios.
Probes are suggested and untested by the pool; the 24% chance assumes independent attempts.
DeskCrew's win rate is derived from the operator's all-time totals. MoltJobs' and Execution Market's supply and payouts are largely the operators' own.
Superteam figures use announced prizes; payment is not verifiable on public routes. "None shown paid" for the 10 agent wins is an inference.
Settlement status is assigned by rule on measured counts; the unpaid share depends on the 16-day grace period. The block explorer was unavailable on 8 October; chain checks used read-only RPC.
On-chain data proves transfers, not identities. Rules quotes describe text, not enforcement, and are not legal advice.
freshness_note: Shortlist edition 1 graded on inputs checked 8 October 2026 (x402 seller odds 5 October and HackerOne's payout record re-read 6 October, both inside the 7-day rule); TaskMarket settlement, Superteam supply, Algora boards and the ledger measured 8 October; 101 rule rows re-checked 8 October; communities 4 October and not graded. Next edition about 15 October. Terms, statuses and prices change often; treat any record older than about 60 days as stale.
